clue.text: Close agreement

definitions.meaning: close as an adjective means packed tightly together, dense
an agreement or treaty between parties, such as a trade pact

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: tightly packed is one meaning, and a formal pact between nations is the other.

clue.text: Praise half the cops on motorway? Correct!

indicators.note: half the asks for the first two of the four letters of the following word

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
to mend is to correct or fix

explanation.surface: Praise for police on the motorway, says an approving voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the' takes CO, the first half of COPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend someone is to praise them formally.

clue.text: With inside condition, feast leads to flab

parts.note: the middle is the inside of something
an age is a stage or condition of life
a spread is a lavish meal or feast

explanation.surface: Combined with an internal disorder, a banquet leads to fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'leads to' only join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the thickening of the waist in later life, so it means surplus fat.

clue.text: Plot to include a rising tax to get workers on time

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or tax
men are workers

explanation.surface: A scheme includes a growing levy so that staff arrive punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the tax in this down light, and 'on' means the workers sit above the time; 'to include' and 'to get' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small rented plot of land for growing vegetables, common in Britain.

clue.text: Judith, on going, displays skimpy underwear

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Judith, while out, shows off scanty lingerie.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a minimal undergarment with a narrow strip at the back.

clue.text: Tasteless place for the poorly?

parts.note: read as a tasteless (sick, as in a sick joke) place to lie (a bed), it is also where an ill person is confined

explanation.walkthrough: A tasteless joke is a sick one, and a bed is a place; together they name where the poorly lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A bed in which an invalid lies while ill is exactly a place for the poorly.

clue.text: It's a canal, crooked and black

indicators.note: crooked says the letters are bent out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: The waterway is twisted and dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges ITSACANAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanical means devilish, so black in the sense of evil.

clue.text: Firm in the red? Just the opposite, I believe

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside another
just the opposite swaps the roles, so the red goes in the firm rather than the firm in the red

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the company in debt? Quite the reverse, I'd say.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, the firm would be in the red; 'Just the opposite' tells you to put the colour inside the company instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Credo is Latin for 'I believe', the opening word of the creed.

clue.text: Shirt I damaged in medical check that is most brutal

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a blood test is a medical check

indicators.note: damaged says the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A shirt was ruined during a medical examination, which was extremely brutal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges SHIRT I, and 'in' places the result inside the medical check, splitting it after its sixth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloodthirstiest means most eager for bloodshed, the superlative of savage cruelty.

clue.text: A French man of letters did, having rushed up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word from bottom to top, so reversed

parts.note: tore means rushed

explanation.surface: A French writer did something in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TORE into EROT. Denis Diderot edited the French Encyclopédie.
explanation.definitionFit: Denis Diderot was an eighteenth-century French philosopher and writer, so a man of letters.

clue.text: In no way extreme position for a dead cat?

definitions.meaning: moderate in opinion, avoiding either political wing
roadkill lies in the centre of the carriageway, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means politically moderate, and literally it is the centre of a street where roadkill lies.

clue.text: Applause for story holding copyright back

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled piece is read in the opposite direction
holding means one piece clasps another inside it

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is the abbreviation for copyright, as in the circled symbol

explanation.surface: A tale wins applause even though it holds a copyright notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts C inside TALE to make TALCE; 'back' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is brilliant success or acclaim, the burst of applause that greets a triumph.

clue.text: Shoot prisoner turning angry with a loud bang

parts.note: to gun is to shoot
POW is a prisoner of war

indicators.note: turning signals that the word for angry is reversed

parts.note: red in the face, so angry

explanation.surface: Someone shoots a prisoner who has turned angry, and there is a loud bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses RED to give DER. The definition is loose: the explosive is what produces a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: The black explosive powder is known chiefly for the loud report it makes when ignited, a definition by association.

clue.text: Localism leads to almost frigid reasoning

parts.note: a dialect is speech local to an area

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: frigid means icy

explanation.surface: Regional speech leads to cold, almost frosty argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of ICY, leaving IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of logical argument, a method of reasoning through opposing positions.

clue.text: Face cleaner you and I hire in a type of bag

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside another

parts.note: a tote is a type of bag
we means you and I
to let is to hire out

explanation.surface: You and I rent a face cloth that comes in a particular bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hire' looks like a verb about renting, but it supplies a three-letter word for letting out property; 'in' wraps the bag round both pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A towelette is a small moist tissue used for wiping the face.

clue.text: Panama doesn't start to show respect

indicators.note: doesn't start says the word for the hat loses its opening letter

parts.note: a Panama is a straw sunhat

explanation.surface: A Panama hat is not raised as a sign of respect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' strips S from SUNHAT. Panama looks like the country, but it is the straw hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhat is to take off one's hat, a traditional gesture of respect or greeting.

clue.text: Fun doesn't start before affair shows apathy

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next
doesn't start means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a concern is an affair or business

explanation.surface: Fun doesn't begin before an affair, which reveals indifference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops F from FUN, leaving UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is a lack of interest or care, which is what apathy means.

clue.text: Taking another course?

definitions.meaning: taking as an adjective means attractive or charming, like the adjective for something cute
a further course of a meal, the pudding served after the main dish

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both charming as an adjective and the dessert course, a British name for pudding.

clue.text: Sink second drink of the cheering brew

parts.note: a cupper, variant spelling of cuppa, is a cup of tea, the cup that cheers

explanation.surface: Have another drink of the cheering brew.
explanation.walkthrough: Tea is traditionally 'the cup that cheers'; CUPPER is a dictionary variant of cuppa.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a ship is to sink it deliberately.

clue.text: Unrestrained wags are very versatile

definitions.note: the definition describes the plural noun, which names things that are very versatile

parts.note: wild means unrestrained
cards are jokers or wags, people who amuse

explanation.surface: Uninhibited jokers turn out to be remarkably adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: wild cards can stand for any card, so they are very versatile.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker or wild card may represent any value in a game, the epitome of flexibility.

clue.text: Differences found in, that is to say, his manuscript

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for that is to say
taken as written

explanation.surface: Discrepancies turn up in, so to speak, his manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Schisms are splits or divisions arising from disagreement.

clue.text: End up with pole bent? That's not settled

indicators.note: bent says the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone ends up with a bent pole and is told that the matter is unresolved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bent' rearranges ENDUP and POLE together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpeopled land has no inhabitants, so it has not been settled by colonists.

clue.text: Entertainment: "The Ring" for every one?

parts.note: a ring is the shape of the letter O
per means for every
a means one

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring cycle as entertainment for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Ring' looks like Wagner's operatic cycle, but it is simply a circle, O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged musical drama, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Good man goes to bed, overturning obligations

indicators.note: overturning turns the whole combined piece upside down in this down light

parts.note: ST abbreviates saint, a good man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A virtuous man goes to bed, tipping over his commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' turns STBED into DEBTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Debts are sums owed, so financial obligations.

clue.text: Nick is not a child

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: Nick insists he is not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A notch is a small cut or nick in an edge.

clue.text: Smart quality of gift fit to go on head

parts.note: a present is a gift
able means fit or capable
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: A gift suitable for wearing on the head gives a smart look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is not a body part but a headland, NESS in place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Being presentable means looking smart and tidy, so the noun is a quality of smartness.

clue.text: Predate new regulations

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the preceding word

explanation.surface: Fresh rules come before their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges the letters of PREDATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Red tape is bureaucratic procedure, the mass of official rules and regulations.

clue.text: Governing bodies showing sense at work

indicators.note: work suggests the letters are put to labour and so moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Legislatures show good sense when they are working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges SENSEAT, with 'at' read as part of the letters and 'showing' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A senate is a legislative chamber, so the plural names governing assemblies.
